headline: Costa Rica Central Bank Buys $1.6 Billion as Dollar Hits Series Low
summary: Costa Rica's central bank purchased over $1.6 billion this year as the U.S. dollar dropped to its lowest price against the colón in the historical series.
why: Central bank interventions in foreign exchange markets aim to manage currency volatility and mitigate the export-damaging effects of rapid local currency appreciation.

impacts.name: Costa Rica
impacts.why: Heavy central bank dollar purchases expand local money supply and attempt to stall currency appreciation.
